Пожелтевшие от времени страницы «Московского Наблюдателя» за 1838 г., «Отечественных Записок» за 1840 г. и «Deutsche Jahrbücher» за 1842 г. сохраняют уже около столетия дерзкие мысли молодого Бакунина. Его предисловие к переводу «Гимназических речей» Гегеля впервые провозгласило на страницах русской печати двусмысленное «примирение с действительностью», незаконченная статья «О философии» видела сущность истинного мировоззрения в искании порядка и бога, а через два года статья в левогегельяноком журнале увенчала гегелевскую диалектику бунтарским лозунгом: «Страсть к разрушению есть творческая страсть». От примирения с действительностью к апологии разрушения — таков путь, пройденный Михаилом Бакуниным за краткий промежуток времени, отделяющий его третью статью от первой; но есть внутренняя логика в этом развитии мысли, развитии столь неожиданном, что даже проницательный Герцен, приветствуя автора революционной статьи, помещённой в «Deutsche Jahrbücher», не узнал в манатом французе Жюле Элизаре своего знакомца и соотечественника. Для того, чтобы вычертить траекторию мысли Бакунина в бурный период (бурный, как вся его жизнь) 1838—1842 гг., необходимо учесть и отметить, что гегельянской пропаганде в Москве и Берлине предшествовало ученичество в Прямухине. 1837 год прошёл для Бакунина под знаком пристального изучения Гегеля. Прямухинские конспекты показывают, как настойчиво углублялся он в энциклопедию абсолютного идеализма, с каким упорством все снова п снова распутывал тройные узлы диалектических хитросплетений. В Москве — кружок Станкевича, бесконечные споры молодых гегельянцев; для Бакунина и Белинского это была подготовка к общественным выступлениям за «примирение с действительностью». «Нет параграфа во всех трёх частях Логики, в двух — Эстетики, Энциклопедии и пр., который бы не был взят отчаянными спорами нескольких ночей», — говорит о кружке Станкевича Герцен в «Былом и Думах»). Первый печатный призыв к примирению с действительностью на основе гегелевской философии был не только личным выступлением Бакунина, но и событием русской общественной мысли, своего рода политической декларацией, а вместе с тем опубликованием тезисов, в значительной мере продуманных членами кружка сообща. «Предисловие переводчика к «Гимназическим речам» Гегеля» начинается резким выпадом против «ужасной, бессмысленной анархии умов, которая составляет главную болезнь нашего нового поколения, — отвлечённого, призрачного, чуждого всякой действительности». Фантастическим, произвольным, небывалым мирам, созданным отвлечённой философией, Бакунин противополагает действительный мир, «естественную и духовную действительность». «До сих пор философия и отвлечённость, призрачность и отсутствие всякой действительности были тожественны; кто занимается философиею, тот необходимо простился с действительностью и бродит в этом болезненном отчуждении от всякой естественной и духовной действительности, в каких-то фантастических, произвольных, небывалых мирах, пли вооружается против действительного мира и мнит, что в осуществлении конечных положений его конечного рассудка и конечных целей его конечного произвола заключается все благо человечества, и не знает, бедный, что действительный мир выше его жалкой и бессильной индивидуальности, не знает, что болезнь и зло заключаются не в действительности, а в нем самом, в его собственной отвлечённости». (М. Бакунин, Предисловие переводчика к «Гимназическим речам» Гегеля, 1838)

Таким образом, русское гегельянство, продолжая борьбу немецкого объективного идеализма с философией субъективизма, уже в первом своём манифесте ополчалось против призрачной отвлечённости мысли, против индивидуализма конечного произвола и ограниченности конечного рассудка, выступая на защиту разумного, а не …

author: Unknown
title: Fredrik Framstegsson - Till en värvad
content:
Författare

: Fredrik Framstegsson

Titel

: Till en värvad

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #11 1915


I.


 Allt lågt som finns i en människas bröst,

 allt uselt och rått, som är,

 kan driva en tanklös och slö individ

 att värva sig till militär


 och bli såsom sådan ett nummer blott,

 ett verktyg, en köpt maskin,

 en marionett - men ett levande liv

 som omskapts av disiplin!


II.


 En

människa

 var du väl dock en gång,

 du broder i brigarens skrud,

 som böjde dig fritt under okets tvång

 för krigets vanskapta gud


 men kanhända du inte förstod det

då

 det du gjorde i ungdomens år...

 Därhemma svalt moder och syskon små;

 på nöden du kunde ej rå!


 Och arbetet tröt och värvarens lock

 förledande ljöd för din själ.

 Så grann är kronans lånade rock

 och hårt är att - svälta ihjäl!


 Då sålde du dig! Sålde själ, sålde kropp

 för att hjälpa i svälthotat hem!

 Du sålde

dig själv

, då i fjättrar du lopp,

 du trodde du gagnade dem,


 dem därhemma, din utslitna far och din mor

 som från barndomen trälat i nöd -

då

 visste du inte vad pina det bor

 i att äta en krigares bröd...


III.


 I långa år han kämpat nog,

 din gamla far, vid harv och plog

 och slitit ut sig själv för andra.

 Den väg han gått var hård och lång

 och nedtryckt utav släpets tvång

 han tröttnade till slut att vandra.


 Bland statarfolket strejk bröt ut

 - man vaknade ändå till slut! -

 och plog och hacka slängdes;

 man hotfullt ställde sig i led

 och gamle far din själv var med

 där allra främst man trängdes.


 De ville hålla fram sin rätt

 på enkelt arbetsmannasätt:

 - » Giv bröd, giv rätt, giv lika! » -

 De skymfades och hotades,

 de bort från gården motades,

 men **ville* ej ge vika.


 Då ljöd ett rop:

"Hit, militär!"

 Bland fredens redskap syns gevär

 och dragna sablar glänsa;

 ett hop soldater tvingats ut,

 utan pardon och utan prut

 från platsen »pöbeln» ränsa.


IV.


 Så står du där då, du som fanan svurit

 och gav dig ut att »skydda hem och härd»,

 du som geväret se'n i blindo burit

 och lärt dig dyrka bajonett och svärd.


 Du ser en hop av fredens män i trasor,

 som önska blott att mänskovärde få,

 som pinats nog av hungersnödens fasor

 och vilja bättre, ljusa villkor nå.


 Du ser dem där. Du ser din ende broder,

 den ende du av många syskon har,

 och bredvid honom ser du så din moder

 och grånad, bruten där din gamle far.


 » Giv akt... ge fyr! » Hör du kommandoorden,

 » ned med det packet!»... Är det väl en dröm? -

 Ditt skott går av och signa ned mot jorden

 du ser en man och utav blod en ström.


V.


 De grånade hårtestar ligga

 i pölen av levrat blod;

 du lärde dig grundligt ditt yrke:

 din träff var god!


 För alltid är den nu slocknad,

 den stämma som var din fars;

 ett dödsskri var sista ljudet

 som fram till ditt öra bars.


Det

 ljudet dock alltid skall klinga

 och isa ditt blod i dess lopp,

 och

du skall förbanna den stundanden

du sålde din själ och din kropp!

«Esas ideas son muy hermosas en teoría pero no son practicables; los nombres necesitan un poder ponderador que los gobierne y obligue a respetar el contrato social». Esa es la última objeción que nos dirigen los partidarios del actual orden social cuando, después de haber discutido, se han quedado sin argumentos y demostrado que el trabajador no puede esperar ninguna mejora sensible para su suerte conservando los mecanismos del actual sistema social.

«Esas ideas son muy hermosas, pero no son practicables; el hombre no está bastante desarrollado para vivir en estado tan ideal. Para ponerlas en práctica sería necesario que el hombre hubiera llegado a la perfección», añaden muchas personas sinceras, pero que, extraviadas por la evolución y la rutina, no ven más que las dificultades y no están bastante convencidos de la idea de trabajar por su realización.

Además, al lado de esos adversarios declarados y de los indiferentes que pueden convertirse en amigos, surge una tercera categoría de individuos, más peligrosos que los adversarios declarados. Esos se fingen entusiastas por las ideas; declaran en alta voz que no hay nada más hermoso; que nada vale la organización actual, que debe desaparecer ante las ideas nuevas, que son el fin al cual debe tender la humanidad, etc., etc. Pero añaden que no son practicables ahora; hay que preparar para ella á la humanidad, guiarla á comprender ese estado dichoso, y con pretexto de ser prácticos, tratan de rejuvenecer esos proyectos de reformas que acabamos de demostrar que son ilusorias; perpetúan las preocupaciones actuales, lisonjeándolas en aquellos á quienes se dirigen, y tratan de sacar el partido mayor posible de la situación actual en beneficio personal, y pronto desaparece el ideal para que lo sustituya un instinto de conservación del actual orden de cosas.

Desgraciadamente, es demasiada verdad que las ideas, objeto de nuestras aspiraciones, no son realizables inmediatamente. Es demasiado ínfima la minoría que las ha comprendido para que tengan influencia inmediata en los acontecimientos y marcha de la organización social. Pero eso no es una razón para no trabajar por realizarla.

Si estamos convencidos de que son justas, debemos tratar de llevarlas á la práctica. Si todo el mundo dice que no son posibles, y acepta pasivamente el yugo de la sociedad actual, es evidente que el orden burgués durará todavía largos siglos. Si los primeros pensadores que lucharon contra la iglesia y la monarquía, por las ideas naturales y por la independencia, y afrontaron la hoguera y el patíbulo, para confesarlas hubieran pensado así, todavía estaríamos en los tiempos de los conceptos místicos y los derechos feudales.

Gracias á que siempre hubo gente que no era práctica, pero que estaba convencida de la verdad, y trataron de hacerla penetrar con todas sus fuerzas por donde pudieron, empezando el hombre á conocer su origen y á deshacerse de las preocupaciones de autoridad divina y humana.
En su libro que realmente vale, Bosquejo de una moral sin obligación ni sanción, desarrolla Guyau, en un capítulo admirable, la siguiente idea: «El que no obra como piensa, no piensa por completo». Es verdad. El que está bien convencido de una idea no puede menos de propagarla y de tratar de realizarla.

Muchas disputas se presencian entre amigos por …

author: Unknown
title: Miguel Amorós - Le mouvement des chômeurs en France
content:
Auteur·e

: Miguel Amorós

Titre

: Le mouvement des chômeurs en France

Sous-titre

: d’un point de vue désabusé

Date

: avril 1998

Notes

: Article publié dans Le Combat Syndicaliste, novembre-décembre 1998. Les deux paragraphes avant le dernier ont été ajoutés ultérieurement par l’auteur. Texte original en espagnol : “El movimiento de parados en Francia visto con desencanto”


 « L’État a toujours fait partie du patrimoine des classes dominantes :

le clergé, la noblesse, la bourgeoisie. A la fin arrive la bureaucratie

quand l’État, ayant épuisé toutes les classes,

tombe ou s’élève, comme on veut, au rang de machine. »

Bakounine


 Actuellement, les faits sociaux sont déterminés par deux formes de domination : l’une directe, crue, sans phrase, matérialiste,

celle du marché

, et l’autre détournée, dissimulée, pleine de discours, idéologique, celle de l’État. L’une parle de « succès » et concerne l’expert, l’autre de « l’intérêt public » et met en avant l’intellectuel. L’une manie l’argent, l’autre manipule la population. L’une achète et l’autre promet. L’une dit « 

ceci est ce que tu as, tu n’as pas le choix

 », l’autre, « 

Suis-moi, je ferai tout ce que tu veux

 ». L’équilibre a été rompu en faveur de la première, ce qui a introduit au fond une réaction conservatrice étatisante, qui veut tirer une légitimité de ceux dont elle cherche à représenter l’intérêt : fonctionnaires, militants, affiliés, électeurs… et fait confiance à l’État comme instrument privilégié pour résister à la logique du marché quand elle nuit à son intérêt. Cette réaction est en train de se transformer en parti, un parti patriotique, qui considère l’État de l’après-guerre comme le représentant de l’intérêt général et le garant du « bien-être » des masses et de « l’indépendance nationale » : « 

le patriotisme est la vertu suprême de l’étatisme

 » (Bakounine). Ce parti définit comme des institutions « publiques » et des piliers de l’État, les organisations et les organismes qui assurent la médiation entre le pouvoir réel et la population : partis, syndicats, ONG, associations, familles… C’est un parti d’intermédiaires (l’État est le lieu adéquat pour la rencontre des intérêts organisés). Sa tactique se fonde sur l’arrêt de la privatisation des services publics, responsable du démembrement de l’État, le contrôle des banques centrales et l’établissement de barrières politiques au marché, comme la semaine des 35 heures, soulageant les déterminations économiques de la fraction étatique de la classe dirigeante dans l’État, la bureaucratie ; cela elle l’appelle l’indépendance de la « nation ». Celle-ci veut prouver qu’elle est encore nécessaire, que sa médiation est bon marché, et elle prétend entretenir sa clientèle par un accroissement de la demande « nationale » provoquée par les dépenses publiques. C’est un parti protectionniste, un parti d’impôts et de tarifs douaniers. Il veut faire entrer dans l’État, grâce à une combinaison économique, une partie du capital qui circule sur le marché.


 En d’autres termes, il veut un nouveau

New Deal

, il préfère faire revenir le monde du travail à feu doux plutôt que de le voir déborder avec une Saint Barthélémy des salaires et des emplois. C’est un parti en herbe, un despotisme cultivé, en France

Le Monde Diplomatique

 est son organe d’expression, Pierre Bourdieu et Ignacio Ramonet en sont les prophètes, en Espagne c’est

El Pais

 avec Joaquin Estefania et Haro Taglen. Ce n’est pas un parti stalinien classique, même si le PCF est une de ses composantes, parce que son discours est le vieux discours de l’ancienne bourgeoisie libérale : démocratie, intérêt national, bien-être, libertés menacées… et que sa stratégie ne passe pas par la conquête de l’État, mais par sa défense à outrance. C’est un front populaire mou. Il s’essaye au style du césarisme latino-américain où l’État joue le rôle historique qui autrefois était dévolu au prolétariat, c’est à dire, être l’agent de la transformation sociale.

Marius et Jeannette

 représentent son prolétariat idéal. Ce n’est pas un parti exclusivement français, nous entendons le même discours en Espagne avec la Gauche Unie, avec les Verts, avec le gauchisme et les groupes spécialisés du genre Mouvement Anti-Maastricht contre la « mondialisation de l’économie », Plate-forme du 0,7 %, Mouvement pour la paix et le désarmement, etc., et même aujourd’hui avec les syndicats et les socialistes. Mais ce parti ne gouverne pas, ne fréquente pas les salons, il est …

title: Peter Kropotkin - Tyskland, den monarkiska principens skyddsvakt
content:
Författare

: Peter Kropotkin

Titel

: Tyskland, den monarkiska principens skyddsvakt

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #44 1916


 Ju mera man studerar det nuvarande krigets uppkomst desto mera förstår man hur oriktigt det är, att söka förklaringen till det i uteslutande ekonomiska orsaker.


 Det är uppenbart, att den tyska bourgeoisien, när den såg Tyskland inträda i en snabb storindustriell utvecklingsfas - en fas som England genomgått efter 1830-talet - ville efterapa England för att på samma sätt göra sig rik i en hast. D. v. s. producera icke blott för det tyska folket, som förblivit allt för fattigt under en junkerfeodalistisk regim, men för export i stor stil. Detta fordrade en stor handelsflotta; en mäktig krigsflotta till dess försvar; en företagsam befolkning duglig till att kolonisera obruten mark, såsom engelsmännen gjort; kolonier i alla delar av världen och lydriken lika så rika och tätt befolkade som Indien och Egyptien för att där kunna avsätta varor, dåliga eller goda.


 Och eftersom Tyskland kom för sent, först då de bästa områdena i Afrika och Asien redan voro beslaglagda, så blir det genom

erövring

 det beslutar att skapa sig ett kolonivälde. Vad skulle det tjäna till att pålägga sig alla utgifter och mödor som följde med kolonisering? - »Frankrikes kolonier erhållas i Paris», hade Bismarck sagt. Paris låg i själva verket endast två till tre dagsresor från Metz och man beräknade att sätta sig i besittning av det genom överrumpling. Och vad det gällde de engelska kolonierna, sade Tirpitz anhängare, skall man få dem genom att skapa en flotta, som är stark nog att mäta sig med Englands. Kol och järngruvor som man behöver för att gjuta kanoner och bygga krigsfartyg skall man finna i norra Frankrike och i de polska provinserna Kielce (de tyska arméerna tillägnade sig i själva verket dessa områden redan vid krigets början.) Det tyska kejsarrikets hamnar skulle bli Triest och kanhända Venedig i Adriatiska havet, Odessa i Svarta havet, och över Bagdad skulle man nå fram ända till persiska viken, efter vilket erövringen av Mindre Asiens fruktbara dalar skulle tillåta en avstjälpning av det tyska befolkningsöverskottet.


 Det är i dessa idéer man uppfostrat en hel generation i Tyskland, ända sedan erövringen av Schleswig-Holstein 1864, krossandet av Österrike 1866 och Frankrike 1871. Och det är dessa idéer som den tyska regeringen slutligen beslöt sig för att realisera, så snart det i 1914 hunnit dra fördel av sin krigsberedskap framför sina grannar.


 Om man vill benämna den militära plundringen, som existerat i alla tider, och »koloniseringen» genom erövring för en »den kapitalistiska utvecklingens ekonomiska lag», så kan man utan tvivel säga, att de »ekonomiska lagarna» framtvingade detta krig. Ni säger, att detta skulle vara en krystad förklaring. Betyder föga! - »Låt oss segra» sa en tysk general i Belgien, »och man skall snart ha glömt resten!»


 Men om den tyska bourgeoisien och en god del av arbetarna, omvända till det man kallar »marxism», delar denna uppfattning, så har en annan del av den tyska bourgeoisien en annan uppfattning, sammanfallande med deras som styra Tyskland. -

»Frankrike med sina revolutioner och sin republik utgör ett farligt jäsningsmedel i Europa»

, sade Bismarck. Det finns beundrare av Tyskland som synes okunniga om detta, men de som ha följt den europeiska politiken känner mycket väl Bismarcks och hans efterföljares ansträngningar att krossa »

denna revolutionära härd

», Frankrike, innan andra nationer följde dess exempel.


 Nyligen påträffade man i Crispotto Crispolti och Guido Aureli verk:

La politiqa di Leone XIII, da Luigi Galimberti a Mariano Rampula, on documenti inediti,

Galimberti hade av påven blivit skickad till Berlin 1877 för att assitera vid Wilhelm I jubileum, och han berättar följande (jag citerar efter den utmärkta ryska historiska revyen, La Voix du passé): »Under loppet av ett samtal om trippelalliansen sade Bismarck mig, att om Italien gav Rom till påven, skulle han, Bismarck, vara mycket glad, ty detta skulle göra Italien mycket starkare, därför att det skulle göra slut på tvedräkten.

Men om han såg att Italien lutade mot den republikanska regimen, och följaktligen mot Frankrike, så skulle han medverka till återupprättandet av kungadömet Neapel

» »Utan att besitta ett territorium, kan det inte finnas någon verklig oavhängighet för honom (påven)», sade Bismarck, »men var …

author: Martha Teodoro
title: Senior citizens endure long wait for promised support
content:
Her experience reflects a fundamental question: Are senior citizens, especially centenarians, actually receiving the support promised to them?

MANILA – Nita Gonzaga, 85, thought all she had to do was wait.

The labor leader from San Andres, Manila had already submitted everything required for the government’s cash incentive for older Filipinos including her birth certificate, a valid ID and a photograph. No medical records. No income certification. The barangay officials handling the process are also senior citizens who know the community well which should hasten the process.

She said that barangay officials collected the documents months ago. But up to now, she has not received the P10,000 (US$164.46) cash gift promised under Republic Act No. 11982 (Expanded Centenarians Act). In fact, she said that none of the members of their senior citizens’ association in Barangay 738 had received this benefit.

Her experience reflects a fundamental question: Are senior citizens, especially centenarians, actually receiving the support promised to them?

For the past three decades, Congress has enacted measures expanding benefits for older Filipinos. Republic Act No. 9994 (Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010) grants senior citizens discounts and tax exemptions on medicines, healthcare, transportation and other essential goods and services. Meanwhile, Republic Act No. 10645 signed into law in November 2014 automatically enrolls all senior citizens in PhilHealth.

Approved in July 2022, Republic Act No. 11916 increased the monthly social pension for indigent senior citizens from P500 to P1,000 ($8.23 to $16.46). And more recently, Republic Act No. 11982 approved in February 2024 expanded government recognition of centenarians by providing P10,000 ($ 164.61) cash gifts to Filipinos upon reaching ages 80, 85, 90 and 95, while retaining the P100,000 ($1,464.09) incentive for those who reach 100 years old.

The expansion of these programs comes as the country’s elderly population continues to increase.

The Philippine Statistics Authority’s 2024 Census of Population reported that the country had 11.42 million senior citizens, representing 10.2 percent of the household population. During roughly the same period, for the May 2022 elections, the Commission on Elections (Comelec) reported about 11.47 million registered senior citizen voters.

According to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), around 4.1 million indigent senior citizens were receiving the Social Pension Program. For its part, the National Commission of Senior Citizens (NCSC) announced that 9.454 million had registered to receive their social benefits. Approximately 75,922 beneficiaries are under the Expanded Centenarians Act.

The PSA estimates the total senior citizen population, Comelec counts registered senior voters, the DSWD tracks social pension beneficiaries, and the NCSC monitors recipients of longevity incentives. These data point to a longstanding challenge raised by advocates and researchers that government agencies continue to maintain fragmented records of older Filipinos.

Judy Taguiwalo, a former DSWD secretary who also taught at the University of the Philippines, said that fragmented data have been the government’s persistent weakness. “Penetration ay isang problema. Ang veracity na information regarding the status of senior citizens,” she said. (Penetration is a problem. And the veracity of information regarding the status of senior citizens.)

She said that the separate databases maintained by local government units, DSWD, NCSC, and other agencies create inconsistencies that can lead to inclusion and exclusion errors in government programs. Some senior citizens appear in one database but not another while others experience delays because records have yet to be validated.

Republic Act No. 11982 attempted to address this problem. Aside from expanding cash gifts for milestone birthdays, the law directed the NCSC to establish an Elderly Data Management System in coordination with the Philippine Statistics Authority, DSWD, Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), and local government units. The system was intended to maintain an integrated database of older persons and beneficiaries, thus improving coordination among agencies and facilitating the implementation of programs. However, the different government statistics indicate that creating a cohesive national overview of the country’s senior citizens is still an …

title: Kosova Başbakanı Kurti'ye mecliste yumurta fırlatıldı
content:
Fotoğraf: Xavier Lejeune/Wikimedia Commons CC BY 4.0

Kosova Başbakanı Albin Kurti'ye Meclis Genel Kurulunda Kosova'nın Geleceği İçin İttifak (AAK) Partisi Milletvekili Time Kadrijaj tarafından protesto amacıyla yumurta atıldı.

7 Haziran'daki erken genel seçimlerin sonuçlarının kesinleşmesinin ardından Kosova Meclisinin yeni başkanı ile yardımcılarını seçmek üzere genel kurul toplandı.

Seçimden birinci çıkan Kendin Karar Al Hareketi'nin (Vetevendosje) Genel Başkanı ve Başbakan Kurti, kürsüde yaptığı konuşmada, diğer siyasi partilerle kurumların oluşturulmasına ilişkin koalisyon görüşmelerinin sürdüğünü belirtti.

Yeni meclis başkanı adayını sunmayan ve görüşmeler için daha fazla zaman talep eden Kurti'nin bu tutumu, diğer siyasi partilerin tepkisine yol açtı. Partiler, Kurti'nin anayasaya aykırı davrandığını öne sürdü.

AAK Milletvekili Kadrijaj, kürsüdeki konuşmasını tamamlayan Kurti'nin yanına giderek çantasından çıkardığı yumurtaları protesto amacıyla fırlattı.

Olayın ardından milletvekilleri arasında kısa süreli gerginlik yaşandı, Meclis Başkanı seçimi için düzenlenen oturum ertelendi.

Kurti, yaptığı açıklamada, yumurtalı protestonun, "diğer partilerle görüşebilmek için ödemesi gereken bir bedelse bunu ödemeye hazır olduğunu" belirtti.

Kosova'da 9 Şubat 2025'te genel seçim, 28 Aralık 2025'te de erken genel seçim düzenlenmişti. Albin Kurti liderliğindeki hükümet, 11 Şubat'ta Meclisten güvenoyu almıştı.

Eski Kosova Cumhurbaşkanı Vjosa Osmani, 5 yıllık görev süresinin sona ermesinin ardından 4 Nisan'da görevini geçici olarak Kosova Meclis Başkanı Albulena Haxhiu'ya devretmişti.

Kosova Meclisi, milletvekillerinin yeni cumhurbaşkanını anayasanın öngördüğü süre içinde seçememesi nedeniyle 29 Nisan'da feshedilmiş, ülkede 7 Haziran'da bir kez daha erken genel seçim yapılmıştı. Meclisin yeni cumhurbaşkanını seçmekte yine başarısız olması halinde ülke, bir kez daha erken genel seçime gidebilir.

title: Iraqi Chief of Staff visits Kirkuk
content:
Iraqi Chief of Staff Abdul Amir Yarallah arrived in Kirkuk accompanied by a high-ranking military delegation. During his visit, Yarallah is expected to hold a series of meetings with military commanders in the city.


According to reports, the discussions will focus on the dissolution of the West of the Tigris Operations Command and proposed organizational changes within the Kirkuk Operations Command.


The West of the Tigris Operations Command was responsible for security in the areas between Kirkuk and Salahaddin provinces, covering the region from the district of Dakuk to Tuz Khurmatu.


The Iraqi Chief of Staff’s visit to Kirkuk comes after Arshad Salihi, head of the Iraqi Turkmen Front in Kirkuk, called for federal forces to maintain their presence in the city.


Salihi argued that if the federal forces were to withdraw from the region, other forces could move in and create new problems.


According to reports, Salihi’s reference to “other forces” was understood to mean the Peshmerga forces.

title: Eren: Democratisation steps must be taken after framework law
content:
The “Bill on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration,” prepared as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, has been submitted to the Presidency of the Grand National Assembly of Turkey.


Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM) Amed MP Serhat Eren spoke to ANF about the Framework Law.


How will the framework law be implemented?


First of all, it is useful to clarify this issue. This bill was first discussed by the Justice Commission. After that, it was approved and then brought before Parliament. The process will be completed by Monday at the latest. After it passes Parliament, the President will approve it, and it will be published in the Official Gazette. Once it has been published in the Official Gazette, there are two important points.


First, the two bodies specified in the law will be established immediately. One of these bodies will be established within the Presidency, namely a coordination office. This coordination office will include the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Interior, the Ministry of National Defence, the General Secretariat of the National Security Council, the General Secretariat of the Presidency, the National Intelligence Organisation (MİT) and the relevant institutions.


Second, a commission will be established within Parliament. Subcommissions may also be established if necessary. The process of establishing these commissions will begin as soon as the law enters into force.


What steps will be taken regarding returns and releases?


PRISONS:


The National Security Council will prepare a report. It will say: “Yes, we have verified it. The weapons have been laid down.” The PKK has dissolved itself and the process of laying down arms will have been completed. The law will enter into force once the relevant report is published in the Official Gazette.


A six-month period will begin from the date on which the National Security Council’s report is published in the Official Gazette. During this six-month period, the process will apply to approximately 3,900 people in prison. Around 900 people will remain in prison. These will be people who have received aggravated life sentences and those who have been involved in killings from 2005 to the present. Everyone else currently in prison will be released.


EXILES:


Those abroad will also be able to apply directly. The person will apply either personally or through a lawyer. They will say, “I will return under this law; I will return to the country.” If their case is at the prosecution stage, the prosecutor’s office will immediately examine the file. It will examine it and say: “Yes, your case falls within the scope of this law. You can benefit from this law and return.”


There are also some people who are considered exceptions under this law. Regarding them, the prosecutor’s office will probably say, “You do not fall within the scope of this law,” or “Your situation falls under the provision defined as an exception, so you cannot benefit from it.” Consequently, they will not return either.


But I can say that 90 percent of those concerned will fall within the scope of the law. A person abroad will apply through their lawyer and will be informed that they can benefit from this law. When they return, they will simply submit their application and the case against them, if it is at the investigation stage, will be postponed.


Of course, when postponing the case, the prosecutor’s office will examine what the allegation in the investigation concerns. If the offence alleged corresponds to a crime for which the Turkish Penal Code prescribes a sentence of more than 15 years, the case will be postponed for 10 years. If it is an offence carrying a sentence of less than 15 years, the case will be postponed for five years. Unless an offence has been committed under the Anti-Terror Law — I am not referring to other ordinary offences, such as traffic accidents — the case will be dropped at the end of five or 10 years.


For those who have been sentenced, or rather those whose cases are before the Court of Cassation or an appeals court, the process will work differently. For detained people whose cases are before the Court of Cassation, the Court of Cassation will directly review their detention status, order their release and send the case back to the local court.

title: A Comuna Amarildo de Souza: Teto, Terra e Território em Santa Catarina
content:
Santa Catarina não é feita apenas por aqueles que tentam apagar sua história de luta. O estado teve Anita Garibaldi, Antonieta de Barros, Cruz e Souza e tantos outros lutadores que construíram uma trajetória de resistência. É nesse espírito que nasce a Comuna Amarildo de Souza, um projeto de reforma agrária que prova que a luta por terra e território está viva e potente em solo catarinense.


Tudo começou em 16 de dezembro de 2013, quando 60 famílias cortaram as cercas de uma área de 900 hectares às margens da SC 401, em Florianópolis. A terra, grilada durante a ditadura militar pelo ex-deputado Artêmio Paludo, não cumpria sua função social enquanto milhares de famílias não tinham onde morar. A ocupação cresceu rapidamente: em uma semana já eram 250 famílias, chegando a 750 ao final de quatro meses, desafiando a especulação imobiliária no "coração do turismo" da capital.


Após despejos, negociações e muita resistência, em julho de 2014 o INCRA destinou às famílias uma área em Águas Mornas. Ali, contra todas as dificuldades, nasceu o primeiro assentamento na modalidade Projeto de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (PDS) de Santa Catarina, com três pilares fundamentais: terra de uso coletivo, produção 100% agroecológica e decisões horizontais em assembleia.


Hoje, a Comuna produz mais de 50 itens agroecológicos, distribuídos semanalmente através de Células de Consumo Consciente em 15 pontos da Grande Florianópolis. Além disso, destinam cerca de 10% da produção para doações a cozinhas comunitárias, ocupações urbanas, comunidades indígenas e quilombolas. Durante a pandemia, doaram aproximadamente 3 toneladas de alimentos.


A agroecologia praticada na Comuna é popular e indissociável da reforma agrária. Como dizem os assentados: "enquanto existir latifúndio no Brasil, todos nós somos sem terra". A produção é da classe trabalhadora para a classe trabalhadora, construindo soberania alimentar, energética e hídrica, e apresentando um modelo capaz de substituir a lógica exploradora do agronegócio.


Após 12 anos de luta, a Comuna Amarildo de Souza segue firme, provando que é possível reflorestar, produzir comida saudável e construir um novo paradigma de organização social em Santa Catarina. A semente plantada em 2013 germinou e continua se espalhando.

title: Armed groups issue threats as deadline expires; Iraqi authorities on alert
content:
Last week, the United States and Saudi Arabia carried out strikes against Hashd al-Shaabi (Popular Mobilization Forces) positions in several Iraqi provinces. The attacks killed 20 fighters and injured 32 others. In response, armed groups in Iraq issued threats, announcing that they would wait until the Arbaeen commemorations of Imam Husseinhad concluded, and that if the Iraqi government failed to respond, they would retaliate themselves.


The deadline set by the armed groups expires today. In a video released by one of the groups, armed men declared: “Listen, Saudis, your time is up. Prepare yourselves. Get your vehicles and equipment ready for rescue. We swear by the Kaaba that we will not rest until we have made you suffer even more.”


Following these threats, the Iraqi Joint Operations Command and security forces held an emergency meeting last night. There are concerns that the armed groups may launch an attack against Saudi Arabia. Several Iraqi officials have called on the groups to exercise restraint and postpone any military action.


In a video message, Hadi al-Amiri, leader of the Fatah Alliance, called on fighters of the Islamic Resistance (Meqawmey Îslamî) to postpone any response to the U.S. and Saudi attacks. Al-Amiri urged the resistance forces to act responsibly, preserve stability in line with Iraq’s higher national interests, delay any attacks, and seek justice for the victims through diplomatic means.


Meanwhile, Kazım Fertusi, spokesperson for Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada, told Rojnews that the Islamic Resistance has so far been waiting to see what measures the Iraqi government will take in response to the Saudi strikes against Hashd al-Shaabi.


The Iraqi government is seeking to keep the armed groups under control by any means necessary and to prevent any attack from being launched from Iraqi territory. Officials are concerned about the consequences, fearing that such an incident could draw Iraq into a major war with unpredictable consequences.


According to security sources, Hashd al-Shaabi officials and the Iraqi government intervened this morning to prevent an attack on a Saudi port. Following the intervention, the Islamic Resistance group decided to postpone its planned retaliation.


Meanwhile, the newspaper Okaz, citing official Saudi sources, reported that intelligence assessments indicate coordination between the Houthis, Iraqi armed groups, and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in preparing for a potential attack against Saudi Arabia.

title: MP Celal Fırat: Alevis want a Turkey where everyone’s rights are guaranteed
content:
With the framework law, a new phase begins in the peace and democratic society process in Turkey. In an interview with ANF, DEM Party MP Celal Fırat explained the expectations of the Alevi community regarding this process. According to Fırat, peace can only be lasting if it is built on democracy, the rule of law, and the equal participation of all segments of society.


Peace is a historical experience for Alevis


According to Fırat, peace holds a special significance for Alevis. He said that the community has endured centuries of discrimination, persecution, and massacres, and therefore welcomes every genuine initiative aimed at achieving a peaceful solution. The silence of weapons, mothers no longer losing their children, and young people experiencing a future instead of war are shared aspirations. However, he emphasized that peace means far more than simply ending armed conflict.


“True peace means strengthening the rule of law, deepening democracy, and ensuring that every person can feel like an equal member of this country. If this process contributes not only to resolving a conflict but also to ushering in a new era of rights, justice, and equality, we will all benefit from it.”


Referring to the Alevi understanding of faith, Fırat pointed to the principle: “Even if you are wronged, do not wrong anyone.”


He said that peace means building a shared future in which no one loses and everyone can live in freedom.


Trust is built through transparency


According to Fırat, many Alevis view the current process with hope, but also with caution. He stressed that this caution does not reflect opposition to peace, but rather the result of historical experience.


“Throughout history, Alevis have repeatedly experienced that promises made to them were not kept. Therefore, we expect this process to be conducted not behind closed doors, but on the basis of parliamentary decisions, the rule of law, transparent procedures, and public participation.”


Fırat said that peace can only be lasting if no one feels excluded from the search for a solution.


“We do not oppose the rights of others. On the contrary, we want a Turkey where the rights of everyone are guaranteed. If any community feels excluded, it will be difficult to build lasting peace.”


Peace and equal rights go hand in hand


According to Fırat, the Alevi community will continue to support the peace process while also maintaining its own democratic demands. These include the legal recognition of Cemevis (Alevi place of worship), unrestricted freedom of religion, and full equality for Alevis. He stressed that these demands are not in conflict with the peace process, but are instead an integral part of a democratic society based on equal rights.


“We want a country where no mother has to bury her child anymore, and no child grows up in fear because of their identity or faith. True peace is achieved when all people can feel equal, safe, and live with dignity.”


In closing, Fırat reaffirmed that the Alevi community will continue to stand on the side of peace, democracy, and human dignity. He said that the words of the Alevi scholar Hacı Bektaş Veli continue to serve as a guiding principle:


“Let us be united, let us be great, and let us be alive.”

title: Murder of Musa Anter: Family files a request to reopen the case
content:
The family of Kurdish journalist and writer Musa Anter, who was killed in 1992 by the Turkish military intelligence unit JITEM, has filed a request to reopen the case. Rahşan Yorozlu, Anter’s daughter, submitted the application through her lawyer Bişar Abdi Alinak to the Department for the Investigation of Unsolved Crimes at the Turkish Ministry of Justice. The aim is to reopen the proceedings, which were dismissed in 2022 due to the statute of limitations. The application calls for a comprehensive reassessment of the case and further investigations to ensure that all those responsible for the killing are held criminally accountable.


New investigation and modern forensic analysis requested


In the application, the family requests that previously omitted investigative measures be carried out and that all evidence collected in the case be reexamined using current forensic and criminal investigation techniques. The applicants also demand a full clarification of the crime and investigations into everyone involved throughout the chain of command. The stated objective is to fully establish the circumstances of the murder and determine the criminal responsibility of all those involved.


Decades without an effective investigation


Musa Anter was murdered on September 20, 1992, in Amed (Diyarbakır). Former JITEM operative Abdülkadir Aygan later stated that Anter had been killed by a unit of which he himself had been a member. Despite this, no effective investigation was carried out for years. It was only after the family brought the case before the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR), which found violations of the right to life in both its substantive and procedural aspects, that the proceedings were reopened. In 2009, 17 years after the murder, the Special Prosecutor’s Office in Amed launched a new investigation based on Aygan’s testimony.


Case dismissed despite confessions


Shortly before the statute of limitations was due to expire, state witness Hamit Yıldırım was arrested in June 2012. A year later, prosecutors indicted Hamit Yıldırım, alleged JITEM operative Mahmut Yıldırım, known by the codename “Yeşil,” Abdülkadir Aygan, and retired Colonel Savaş Gevrekçi on charges of premeditated murder and other offenses.


In 2015, the case was transferred from Amed to Ankara on security grounds, where it was merged with the so-called main JITEM trial. On September 21, 2022, Ankara’s 6th High Criminal Court dismissed the case on the grounds that the statute of limitations had expired.


With the newly submitted application, the family is making a renewed legal effort to fully clarify the murder of Musa Anter and to hold those responsible accountable, despite the dismissal of the original proceedings.

title: MHP’s Fethi Yıldız reads Öcalan’s February 27 call at parliamentary committee session
content:
The “Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion,” prepared as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process and submitted to the Speaker of Parliament on August 5 with the signatures of 360 MPs, is being discussed in the Parliamentary Justice Committee.


The committee session began with opening remarks by Justice Committee Chair Cüneyt Yüksel, followed by a presentation of the bill by the ruling AKP Deputy Chair Abdulhamit Gül.


Speaking afterward, MHP (Nationalist Movement Party) Deputy Chair Fethi Yıldız shared his assessment of the proposal. Recalling MHP Chair Devlet Bahçeli’s earlier call to Abdullah Öcalan, Yıldız said that a new era has begun in Turkish politics.


During his speech, Yıldız read Öcalan’s “Call for Peace and Democratic Society” issued on February 27, 2025, and recalled that the PKK dissolved itself after the call.


Yıldız continued: “Weapons were burned in a ceremony. That marked a new phase, followed by the establishment of the parliamentary committee. Now a temporary law has been prepared. The law is important for unity and does not open the way to amnesty or impunity. It also includes the verification and documentation of the surrender of weapons and military inventories. This temporary law will strengthen the rule of law in Turkey. As the MHP, we are committed to safeguarding the brotherhood that has existed for thousands of years. Our Kurdish brothers and sisters are an integral part of the Turkish nation. We do not want to carry any more coffins on our shoulders.”


At times, the committee’s deliberations were interrupted by heated exchanges and arguments.

title: Turkish national on wanted list appointed division commander in Syria
content:
The Syrian transitional authorities have appointed Turkish national Ömer Muhammed Çiftçi as commander of the 62nd Division.


The appointment has drawn attention because of the agreement reached on January 29 between the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and the transitional government, which provides for the removal of non-Syrian fighters from the country.


Born in Osmaniye, Turkey, in 1980, Ömer Muhammed Çiftçi operated under the aliases Muhtar Türki and Umar Mohammed Jaftashi. He joined al-Qaeda in Afghanistan in 2004 and later traveled to Syria in 2012, where he joined the HTS (Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham).


Çiftçi had previously been included on Turkey’s Ministry of Interior’s most wanted list because of his alleged links to al-Qaeda. Ankara removed him from the wanted list after HTS came to power in Syria in December 2024.

title: Iranian forces arrest seven Kurdish citizens in Marivan and Kamyaran
content:
Iranian forces have arrested at least seven Kurdish citizens – Jamal Rostami, Saman Khosravi, Hawre Parvazeh, Arya Maroufi, Zanyar Asvar, Peshtiwan Tatar, and Saro Roshani – in Marivan and Kamyaran in Kurdistan Province and taken them to undisclosed locations.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Iranian security forces surrounded the village of Ney in Marivan with several military vehicles in the early hours of 6 August, raiding residents’ homes and arresting Khosravi, Parvazeh, Maroufi, Asvar, Tatar and Roshani.


The six men were arrested without warrants, and no information has since been obtained about their fate or whereabouts.


Two days earlier, in the early hours of 4 August, Ministry of Intelligence forces raided an orchard belonging to Jamal Rostami, a resident of Shahini village in Kamyaran and a founding member of a local charity organisation, and arrested him without a warrant.


At around 14:00 (local time) the same day, the forces returned to the orchard, intimidated Rostami’s family and searched the premises.


Two other founding members of the charity, Esmaeil Khateri and Foad Shadi, had previously been arrested by security forces on 24 and 25 July respectively. No information has since been obtained about their fate or whereabouts.

title: The experience of local democracy in Kurdistan
content:
For decades, local democracy in Kurdistan has been subjected to intense repression by the Turkish state. The people's struggle to exist with their language, identity, and culture has been met with repression, arrests, the appointment of trustees, and bans. The domination imposed over local governments—one of the key pillars of local democracy—reveals the state's monolithic and authoritarian approach to governance. According to this understanding, the more local democracy is suppressed, the more effectively the people's demands for rights can be eliminated.


In response, the Kurds have built upon the experience they accumulated since the 1970s and continued this effort since 1999. Beginning with HADEP and deepening through DEHAP, DTP, and BDP, this 27-year process sought not only to win municipal administrations but also to establish a model of governance that touched people's daily lives, preserved their identity and culture, and placed women's liberation and ecological balance at its center. This model evolved through successive stages, including people-oriented municipalism, multilingual public services, the co-mayor system, and democratic autonomy.


H

ADEP: People-oriented municipals


The 1999 local elections marked a turning point for the Kurds. HADEP won 37 municipalities, including the Amed Metropolitan Municipality, as well as Ağrı, Batman, Bingöl, Hakkari, Siirt, and Wan. For a people who had endured years of enforced disappearances, detentions, and repression, this victory became a powerful source of hope. HADEP adopted a model it called "People-Oriented Municipalism," whose main objective was to provide public services, strengthen infrastructure, and combat poverty.


Practical measures were implemented rapidly. Women's centers, public laundries, and communal bread-baking houses were established to meet everyday needs. Green spaces were created, and efforts were made to preserve historical heritage. The election of Ayşe Karadağ in Derik, Cihan Sincar in Kızıltepe, and Mukaddes Kubilay in Bazîd represented important advances for women's political representation.


The Turkish state, however, did not tolerate these developments. Following the elections, the mayors of Amed, Siirt, and Bingöl were detained, and thousands of people who participated in street protests were arrested. A closure case was filed against HADEP, and the party was dissolved in 2003. This marked the beginning of what would become systematic policies of repression and political elimination in the years ahead.


DEHAP: Multilingual and women-centered municipalism


Following HADEP's closure, the Kurdish political movement reorganized under DEHAP. In the 2004 local elections, it formed democratic alliances under the umbrella of the Social Democratic People's Party (SHP), increasing the number of municipalities it controlled.


During the DEHAP period, the concept of "Multilingual and Women-Centered Municipalism" was adopted. Providing services in Kurdish and other mother tongues, strengthening women's commissions, and expanding social projects became central priorities.


Multilingual municipal services were introduced in places such as Sur, Adana, and Cizîr. Women's quotas were implemented, while the number of women's councils and women's centers increased. Conferences adopted decisions on issues ranging from poverty and the economy to culture and services for people with disabilities. Public spaces where residents could gather were created, while support for cultural activities was significantly expanded. This period represented an effort to transform municipalities from mere service providers into instruments of broader social transformation.


The state's response remained harsh. Facing the threat of closure, DEHAP dissolved itself, paving the way for the establishment of DTP. Arrests, detentions, and administrative obstacles continued throughout this period. The nation-state mentality portrayed multilingualism and women's liberation as forms of "separatism," targeting the gains achieved by the people.


DTP: Democratic Autonomy and the co-mayor system


The establishment of DTP in 2005 marked the beginning of a new phase. The party incorporated the model of "Democratic Autonomy" into its statutes and reorganized local governments accordingly. The model aimed to strengthen local democracy and place the people's will at the center of governance. It proposed a decentralized system that would expand the authority of local governments …

title: Koçyiğit: Öcalan’s call is a call for a great Middle East peace
content:
Political parties’ assessments of the bill discussed in the Parliamentary Justice Commission under the title “Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration” continue. The commission meeting began with a speech by Justice Commission Chair Cüneyt Yüksel and continued with AKP Deputy Chair Abdulhamit Gül presenting the bill.


Speaking at the commission, Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Group Deputy Chair Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit stated that 2026 was an important year for all segments of society in Turkey and that Turkish politics was going through a critical period. Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit said: “Today is an important day and we are witnessing history. We are part of history and its primary actors. In this sense, we are not simply discussing a proposal. We are also discussing together how we will build our common future, how we will live together and how our lives will take shape from now on. We are at an important threshold. If we cross this threshold strongly, we will have taken significant steps towards building an equal, free and democratic republic with strong steps for tomorrow. We want to state that every person in this country who stands for equality and freedom faces a historic responsibility. We are not here merely as members of parliament; we also represent millions of people living in this country. We want to fulfil our responsibility towards these millions by bringing them one step closer to a solution and peace. As DEM Party, for the first time we are speaking in Parliament and in a commission as the first signatories and owners of a proposal. This proposal is an important beginning, a seal placed on our common future that will keep us together.”


The borders created by imperialists are disappearing


Adding that the borders established in the Middle East by imperialist states 100 years ago are disappearing, Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit continued: “The global capitalist system is being reshaped, and violence plays the most dominant role in this reshaping. Unfortunately, the fate of the peoples of the Middle East has always been to become victims of this violence. We believe that wars, occupations, massacres and what has happened in the Middle East should teach and reveal a reality, a truth, to each and every one of us. In 2026, before the eyes of the whole world, we all witnessed the genocide and massacre in Palestine that actually began much earlier. It happened in front of the eyes of the world. We witnessed a great genocide in which, even according to official figures, 70,000-80,000 people lost their lives. What lies behind all these genocides and massacres? There are energy routes, trade routes, and the desire to dominate these energy and trade routes. In this sense, capital and power are reshaping global geopolitics in the hands of a single authority.”


Mr Öcalan’s intervention


Koçyiğit added: “Unfortunately, what falls to the peoples here is death, blood, tears and exile. We can even add to this the children who died of hunger in Palestine and Gaza. So, what position does Turkey hold at the centre of this upheaval in the Middle East, where the 100-year-old status quo is being disrupted and the borders drawn by imperialist states a century ago are being overturned? How will Turkey build its future? We must not forget that with this law today, we are also providing an answer to this question.


The Al-Aqsa Flood marks a major breaking point in the history of the Middle East. What does the Middle East need? Is it war? Is it the division of borders on an ethnic basis? Or does the Middle East actually need the construction of an equal and free life based on the participation of peoples? Of course, it is the second. Within this great upheaval, we see that Mr Öcalan’s Peace and Democratic Society Call on 27 February represents a major intervention in favour of the peoples into this historical course.”


This call is a call for a great peace 


Koçyiğit said that “this call is not only a call that opens the door to a new era in Turkey; it can also be regarded as a call for a great Middle East peace, a call for a great Middle East transformation in which peoples live together as equals and in freedom. The Peace and Democratic Society Process is in fact an intervention into history in favour of peoples. It is an intervention into the flow of history in favour of all oppressed, denied, marginalised, excluded and disregarded social groups, peoples and faiths. It is a great manifesto …

title: Abdullah Aysu: The way out for agriculture is democratic, producer-oriented cooperatives
content:
Turkey’s agricultural sector has come under increasing scrutiny in recent years due to rising production costs, climate-related risks and fluctuations in production. According to data from the Turkish Statistical Institute (TÜİK), crop production fell by 5 percent in 2024 compared with the previous year, declining to approximately 75.5 million tonnes due to a decrease in cereals and other field crops. By contrast, vegetable production increased by 5.6 percent to 33.6 million tonnes, while production of fruit, beverage and spice crops rose by 2.1 percent to 28 million tonnes.


Producers frequently highlight the negative impact on production of rising costs for essential agricultural inputs, particularly diesel, fertiliser, animal feed, seeds and pesticides. Especially in Kurdistan, many farmers are trying to pay off their debts by selling their agricultural land because of rising prices and costs.


Commenting on the difficulties farmers have been experiencing recently, Abdullah Aysu, Honorary President of the Farmers’ Union (Çiftçi-Sen), said agriculture in Turkey has declined as a result of free-market policies, arguing that the solution is democratic, producer-oriented cooperatives.


Aysu said Turkish agriculture had faced structural problems for many years and that the policies being implemented were putting producers in a difficult position. He said: “Turkish agriculture has been continuously deteriorating since 1980. The main reason for this is that agriculture was left to the free market. The state’s agricultural support institutions were privatised. Once these institutions disappeared, farmers were left to face companies directly,” Aysu said.


Farmers are abandoning production because of costs


Pointing to the way the industrial agricultural model has increased producers’ costs, Aysu said: “Because the agricultural system has been transformed into industrial agriculture, production inputs are supplied by companies. Since there are no longer public institutions to regulate the market, input prices increase every year. At the same time, the prices of agricultural products are set low. As a result, farmers are constantly making losses and eventually give up production.”


The way out of this crisis is organisation


Aysu said the solution to the problems facing agriculture lies in organised production, and added: “Just as every problem has a way out, this one does too. Society needs to organise itself economically, socially and independently. Cooperatives are an ideal model for this. Cooperatives need to be effective not only in production but also in marketing. Farmers should not sell their products as raw materials. They should process their products, create added value and market them through cooperatives. This would eliminate intermediaries, leaving the share they take with the producers. In this way, it would be possible to overcome costs and Turkish agriculture could become stronger again.”


There is a lack of democratic functioning


Abdullah Aysu also said that cooperatives in Turkey had failed to achieve the expected success, arguing that the reason was a lack of democratic functioning. He added: “The reason cooperatives have not been very successful so far is that they have been established from the top down. Producers become alienated from cooperatives because they have no say or decision-making power. Cooperatives need to be genuinely established and managed by producers. Presidents should not be elected for a second term, and the profits generated must be distributed fairly among the members.”

title: Iran attacks Rojhilat parties
content:
Emced Hisên Pena, a member of the Central Committee of the Community of Kurdistan Workers, said that the Iranian regime had carried out a comprehensive attack with kamikaze drones targeting the bases of parties from Rojhilatê Kurdistan.


Speaking to the Rojnews news agency, Emced Hisên Pena said that the home of one of the members working at their party’s political academy in the Bangewre area near Zirguwêz was also targeted in the attack.


Emced Hisên Pena said there were no casualties in the attacks.


In the war between the US-Israel and Iran that began in February 2026, the Iranian regime has carried out more than 960 attacks against South Kurdistan using missiles and armed drones.


More than 30 people have reportedly been killed and around 160 injured in these attacks.

title: DEM Party: We will continue our struggle to build the law of the future
content:
Debate on the bill titled “Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration,” submitted to the Parliamentary Justice Commission, has concluded. The commission adopted the bill. Representatives of political parties continued to take the floor on Article 9 of the 12-article bill.


DEM Party Justice Commission members Zülküf Uçar, Onur Düşünmez and Newroz Uysal Aslan also spoke about the provisions of the law.


Zülküf Uçar said the bill represented, for them, a historic window in which the Kurdish people’s struggle for existence and the state’s need for transformation intersected, and continued: “We consider this window to be a rich space in favour of democracy and freedoms. What matters now is to cultivate this space through a common will and put it on track towards a common future. In this sense, each of us has assumed an important responsibility. This law should be regarded as a law of commitment. It is a text that commits to Turkey’s democratic future. It is a text that commits to bringing the Kurdish people, with all their existence and rights, within the framework of the law. This text is the first step on the ladder leading towards the rule of law, freedom of expression and the vision of a democratic society.


As a requirement of the rational and natural dynamics of the search for integration, exceptional provisions should be removed from the text, and the text should be revised to encompass everyone. During this dynamic period in history, when major responsibilities have been assumed, continuous legislative activity until a final solution is reached should be the defining characteristic of the process. The laws that follow will be the lifeblood of this strategic process. Immediately after the first step being built today, we need to take the step towards the second.


“Resolving all these problems is the moral and legal responsibility of each and every one of us. As we know, in human creations, perfection is an ideal that can never be fully attained. Of course, this law is not perfect either, but it is historic. As a requirement of its historic character, we can address some of its shortcomings right here. First of all, we need to make the ambiguous content of Article 3 more explicit. We can begin by clarifying the scope of the phrase ‘the offence of intentional killing committed within the framework of organisational activities’ currently contained in the article. Because, as is known, when general principles of criminal law are applied to the elements of an offence, they become part of it, and this may lead to serious differences of interpretation in practice.


“Another issue concerns confiscation. Resorting to confiscation during the investigation and prosecution stages would constitute a serious violation of the presumption of innocence. For this reason, removing confiscation from the scope of this article is important for the legality and consistency of the law. Moreover, defining assets subject to confiscation through broadly interpretable concepts such as ‘goods and assets’ is not compatible with the general spirit of the law. This shortcoming also needs to be addressed.


Another issue that needs to be revised in the text of the article is contained in the third paragraph. Investigations concerning offences committed before the publication of the National Security Council decision but initiated after its publication are made subject to the board’s permission. However, when the six-month application period is taken into account, it becomes clear that this creates significant risks in practice. An investigation opened with the board’s permission after the six-month period has expired will not have any guarantee under this law. This problem, which is incompatible with the principle of the rule of law, must also be resolved. Our proposal regarding this paragraph is for the period stipulated in Article 9 to begin from the date on which the matter becomes known. If we address these shortcomings, we will have brought the law into a form consistent with its purpose and spirit.”


The law is a beginning


“This law is a beginning,” Onur Düşünmez said, adding: “The value of the step taken today lies in the fact that it opens the way for the steps that will follow. Everyone here, regardless of their political views, must approach such an issue, where the fate of peoples is at stake, with common sense. This issue goes far beyond short-term political calculations, narrow party interests and the reflex of …

author: Unknown
title: Tamir: Prisons have become centres of rights violations
content:
As concerns over the right to life of seriously ill prisoners in prisons grow by the day, the government’s failure to take concrete steps in this regard despite urgent calls for their release from lawyers, human rights defenders and civil society organisations has drawn criticism. The release of many sick prisoners whose treatment cannot be adequately maintained under prison conditions is being prevented through various administrative and political practices, despite the absence of any provision in execution legislation that would prevent their release.


In particular, reports by the Forensic Medicine Institute and decisions by the Administrative and Monitoring Boards, as well as assessments that prisoners “pose a risk to public security” or “are capable of maintaining their lives independently in prison,” are cited among the main obstacles preventing seriously ill prisoners from regaining their freedom.


Ahmet Tamir, who was released from prison after 30 years of incarceration, spoke to our agency about rights violations in prisons and the situation of sick prisoners.


A system targeting human dignity is in place


Tamir said prisons have been turned into places where severe rights violations occur, adding that “practices in prisons are compatible neither with international human rights standards nor with Turkey’s own laws. An entirely arbitrary approach to governance prevails. Everyone puts themselves in the place of the prosecutor, judge and decision-making authority. Even the most basic human right, the right to speak your mother tongue, is prohibited. You are prevented even from living according to your identity. You are openly subjected to the mentality that says, ‘If you submit, everything is permitted; if you don’t, you cannot even access your most basic needs.’ The prosecutor approves the prison’s decision, and the court then finds the prosecutor’s decision to be correct. In this way, rights violations become institutionalised. This is no longer simply a matter of violating the law; it is a system that targets human dignity.”


Ill prisoners are deliberately deprived of treatment


Pointing out that sick prisoners face the most severe conditions in prisons, Tamir said that deliberate delays are imposed even in urgent medical situations. He said that even in emergencies, calling an ambulance is delayed on various pretexts, adding: “They waste hours asking questions such as where the patient is in pain and which medication they are taking. Yet instead of providing urgent medical intervention, they deliberately waste time so that the illness becomes more severe. This is a deliberate practice. Prisoners referred to hospital are subjected to demands that they be examined while handcuffed. This effectively eliminates their right to receive treatment; they are told, ‘Either you will be examined in handcuffs or you will not be treated.’”


The aim is not to treat, but to slowly wear a person down


Tamir said that the policies implemented in prisons target not only physical but also psychological destruction, and continued: “Rather than abandoning a person directly to death, they try to consume them drop by drop. They aim to destroy their freedom of thought, will and hope. This is an inhumane mentality. The Forensic Medicine Institute says someone is ‘unfit’, while another doctor says they are ‘fit’. The hospital makes one decision, the prison administration makes another. It is unclear which decision is valid. Because everyone sees themselves as the sole authority. The mentality of ‘I am the power here, my decision is the one that counts’ prevails. Even prisoners in serious health conditions are given reports stating that they ‘can maintain their lives in prison’. This approach violates human dignity.


In particular, the Administrative and Monitoring Boards postpone the release of prisoners who have completed their sentences on various grounds. A prisoner whose sentence has ended can be given a three- or six-month postponement of release by being told, ‘You have consumed too much water.’ Yet water is already provided in limited quantities in prisons. These grounds cannot be explained in legal terms. The real aim is to undermine a person’s morale, destroy their hope and break their will. Practices that are an extension of special warfare policies are in operation in prisons. You are forced to use certain terms. If you use the expressions they want, they issue a report saying that you have been ‘rehabilitated’ …

author: Rheinmetall Entwaffnen Berlin
title: Montag, 17. August 2026 * 18:30 Uhr Onboarding für Neue * 19:00 Uhr Plenum * NewYorck Bethanien * Berlin-Kreuzberg
content:
Bei unserem Treffen am 17. August werden wir zunächst Organisatorisches für die kommenden Wochen und insbesondere für das Protestcamp in Köln, das vom 01. – 06.09.2026 stattfindet, besprechen.


Nach dem Plenum ist geplant, sowohl für das Rheinmetall Entwaffnen Camp in Köln als auch in Hamburg plakatieren zu gehen.


Kommt dafür am Montag, den 17. August 2026 um 18:30 Uhr ins NewYorck Bethanien, Mariannenplatz 2a, 10999 Berlin-Kreuzberg, 2. Etage.


Oder schreibt uns eine E-Mail: rheinmetall-entwaffnen-berlin@riseup.net


Wer sind wir?


Seit 2018 organisiert Rheinmetall Entwaffnen regelmäßig kleine und große Aktionen gegen Aufrüstung, Abschottung, Waffenproduktion und Rüstungsexporte. Wir sind ein bundeseites Bündnis, das in vielen Städten lokal verankert ist. In Berlin kommen wir alle zwei Wochen zusammen. Wir diskutieren auf unseren Treffen aktuelle Entwicklungen, vernetzen uns mit anderen Aktivst:innen, planen Veranstaltungen, Aktionstage, Aktionswochen und natürlich auch Camps.


Unsere Motivation und unser gemeinsames Ziel ist es, der Aufrüstung und militärischen Zuspitzung durch aktives Handeln was entgegenzusetzen und im besten Fall zusammen aufzuhalten. Denn: Kriege nützen den Reichen, wir liefern die Leichen. Wir wollen den Kapitalismus überwinden, um die Ursachen und fatalen Folgen von Krieg und Elend abzuschaffen. Wir kämpfen für eine solidarische Welt, ohne Ausbeutung, Unterdrückung und Krieg.

title: Laïcité coloniale et lois d'exception en Afrique française
content:
Texte paru dans le numéro 1878 du magazine mensuel de la Fédération Anarchiste (

FA

) «

 

Le Monde Libertaire

 

» sur le 120

e

 anniversaire de la loi du 9 décembre 1905 concernant la séparation des Églises et de l'État.


Le 120

e

 anniversaire de la loi du 9 décembre 1905 concernant la séparation des Églises et de l'État nous permet de revenir sur une histoire jalonnée d'exceptions. Nous l'avons évoqué notamment avec l'historien Sadek Sellam que nous avons invité plusieurs fois durant notre émission «

 

Médias et antifascisme

 

» présente tous les deuxièmes vendredis du mois sur Radio Libertaire à 11h30. L'application à géométrie variable de la laïcité française nous montre ainsi que le culte musulman en Algérie et aux colonies fit l'objet d'un dirigisme troublant de la part de l'État.


L'émission «

 

Médias et antifascisme

 

» que nous animons sur Radio Libertaire tous les deuxièmes vendredis du mois à 11h30 depuis le 11 octobre 2024 s'est penché plusieurs fois sur des sujets liés à la laïcité. Avec l'historien Sadek Sellam, nous nous sommes employés à analyser les applications bancales de la loi du 9 décembre 1905 jusqu'à nos jours. Nous avons ainsi évoqué à partir du 14 mars 2025 la gestion en France du culte musulman notamment à travers le cas de la grande mosquée de Paris.


Cette institution inaugurée en 1926 met ainsi en valeur une gestion coloniale et dirigiste d'un culte considérée à la fois comme exotique et dangereux. La mosquée a en effet été inaugurée presque trois ans après la création par le conseil municipal de Paris d'une «

 

section d'affaires indigènes nord-africaines

 

». Le maréchal Hubert Lyautey à cette époque «

 

résident général de la République au Maroc

 

» avait ainsi été consulté pour un projet d'institut musulman imaginé initialement par le professeur Paul Bourdarie.


Ce dernier enseignait au collège libre des sciences sociales, dirigeait la revue «

 

Indigène

 

» et voulait mettre «

 

en contact les jeunes éléments les plus cultivés de l'islam avec la fleur de la science et de la société française

 

». Si la mosquée a pu voir le jour, le projet d'institut fut allègrement saboté par Lyautey qui craignait sa possible influence sur les «

 

jeunes musulmans

 

»

 [

1

]

. L'État versa tout de même à cet institut purement fictif des subventions jusqu'en décembre 1980. Une «

 

commission nationale des français musulmans

 

» présidée par le secrétaire d'État aux rapatriés Jacques Dominati venait en effet de montrer le non-fonctionnement de cet institut.


Un autre exemple du non-respect de la laïcité par le gouvernement fut la nomination de Hamza Boubakeur au poste de recteur de la mosquée de Paris le 18 mai 1957. Ce dernier était hostile à l'indépendance de l'Algérie et faisait selon le chef du gouvernement Guy Mollet mieux l'affaire qu'Ahmed Benghabrit.


Celui-ci avait succédé à son oncle Kaddour qui dirigeait la mosquée depuis sa création. Il fut ainsi «

 

limogé

 

» pour avoir refusé de coopérer avec le commissariat de police du cinquième arrondissement de Paris où se situe la mosquée. Son refus de lutter contre le Front de Libération Nationale (

FLN

) algérien et sa dénonciation de la torture poussa Mollet à nommer à sa place un homme aux ambitions politiques bien trempées.


Boubakeur cherchait en effet à partir de 1960 à devenir le président d'une République saharienne qui aurait été issue de la séparation du Sahara du reste de l'Algérie. Ce plan de participation soutenu par le premier ministre français Michel Debré tomba finalement à l'eau. La nomination de Boubakeur à la tête de la mosquée de Paris fut elle condamnée en 1963 par le tribunal administratif de Paris. Cela n'empêcha pas Boubakeur de rester à son poste jusqu'en 1982 avant que l'Algérie ne prenne le relais de la France dans le versement de subventions à la mosquée de Paris

2

]

.


La laïcité inexistante en Algérie et en Afrique Occidentale Française

des règlements d'administration publique détermineront les conditions dans lesquelles la présente loi sera applicable à l'Algérie et aux colonies
